notes:
Section heading is "West Coast of Scotland." with three sub-headings: "Mainland." (81-82), "Outer Hebrides." (83-88) and "Mainland, Skye, and Inner Hebrides." (89-120). I've written coast as "West Coast of Scotland--<sub-heading>" because a bare "Mainland" would get confused with Orkney or Shetland. The other column holds the height in feet of the centre of the light above water, as printed. Only Cape Wrath has "ft." after its figure.

How I copied:
- Fragments are exact copies of each printed line, with only the leading indentation and the number's full stop removed. Inner spacing is kept.
- Names and places keep their printed punctuation, in the style of your "Farn, Inner," example: "Cape Wrath.", "Rona," + "Skye.".
- For keepers I dropped the full stop that ends each row ("John M'Gill." became "John M'Gill"). Restore it if you want that copied too.
- "italic" means the name and place sit inside _..._. The underscores are left out of name and place but kept in the fragments.

Rows to check:
- 86 Monach Island: the brace groups two heights, Upper 150 and Lower 62 (two lights), and spans lines 2955-2956. It doesn't group stations, so marks is just "**".
- 93/94 Hynish Signal Tower and Skerryvore: these are numbered separately but joined by a brace and have no return mark. The height 150 and the keeper William Crow are printed only on line 2967. They probably belong to the pair, since Hynish was Skerryvore's shore signal station and 150 ft fits Skerryvore's light rather than a signal tower. I put them on row 93 because that's where they're printed. Mark "{ }" stands for the brace.
- 99 Fladda and 101 M'Arthur's Head are marked both * and italic. By the legend that's a contradiction: * means returns came this year, italics means they came last year but not this year. It's copied as printed.
- 119 Bahama Bank: the row has "1880.--" (added this year), "*", "(L.V.)" with the ‡ footnote mark, and "--" where the height would be. That fits the footnote: light-vessel heights aren't given. The keeper is printed only as "Johns.", which may be a surname or a shortened form. I kept "Johns".
- 120 Langness: "1880.--Langness Lighthouse, do." I split "Lighthouse" off as the type, which lost the comma after it. "do." means ditto, i.e. Isle of Man. It has no height, keeper or mark.

Spellings copied unchanged (likely modern or correct forms in brackets): "Rosspire" (probably a misprint for Ross-shire), "Island Glass" (Eilean Glas), "Rhu Stoir" (Rhu Stoer), "Dhuheartach" (Dubh Artach), "Rhuvaal" (Ruvaal), "Lochindaul" (Loch Indaal), "Skervuile", "Chickens Rock" (Chicken Rock), "Argyleshire", "Loch Eil" (Corran Ferry is on Loch Linnhe at the mouth of Loch Eil). No light characters are given in this list.
